concepts.name: IDA's Institutional Identity and World Bank Group Architecture
key_dimensions: IDA vs IBRD: differentiation by borrower eligibility, lending terms, and funding sources
IDA's position within the five World Bank Group institutions (IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID)
IDA as a legally separate entity yet operationally integrated with IBRD — the 'shared services' model
UPSC trap: IDA is NOT the same as World Bank; World Bank = IBRD + IDA only

concepts.name: IDA Establishment, Founding Purpose, and Governance Structure
key_dimensions: Year of establishment (1960) and the gap it filled after IBRD's commercial-rate lending proved inaccessible to poorest nations
Headquarters location (Washington D.C.) and relationship with IMF headquarters — proximity trap
Governance: Board of Governors, Board of Executive Directors, President (shared with IBRD)
Voting power structure: shareholding vs. IDA replenishment contribution linkage

concepts.name: IDA Eligibility Criteria for Borrowing Countries
key_dimensions: Primary threshold: GNI per capita below the 'operational cutoff' (updated periodically, ~$1,315 in IDA20 cycle)
Creditworthiness criterion: inability to access international capital markets on reasonable terms
Blend countries: nations eligible for both IDA and IBRD simultaneously (e.g., India was a blend country)
Graduation from IDA: process, reverse graduation concept, and recent examples — UPSC trap on India's graduation

concepts.name: IDA Financial Instruments: Credits, Grants, and Guarantees
key_dimensions: IDA Credits: concessional loans with near-zero to zero interest (service charge ~0.75%), long maturities (25–40 years), grace periods (5–10 years)
IDA Grants: given to most debt-vulnerable countries — no repayment obligation; distinction from credits is a frequent trap
Scale-Up Facility (SUF) and Private Sector Window (PSW): non-concessional and blended finance instruments introduced in IDA18
Guarantees under IDA: credit and political risk guarantees to crowd in private investment

concepts.name: IDA Replenishment Process: Mechanism and Significance
key_dimensions: Replenishment cycle: every 3 years; donor countries negotiate commitments (IDA19, IDA20, IDA21 — current cycle)
IDA20 theme: 'Finance for a Livable Planet' — focus areas, replenishment size (~$93 billion record)
IDA21 negotiations: launched 2024, focus on climate, fragility, and private capital mobilization
Internal resource generation: reflows from loan repayments + IBRD transfers + market borrowings now supplement donor contributions

concepts.name: IDA's Market Borrowing Capability and AAA Credit Rating
key_dimensions: IDA18 (2017) marked the first time IDA was authorized to borrow from capital markets — structural shift
AAA credit rating from major agencies despite lending to high-risk countries — the 'preferred creditor status' mechanism
Implications: IDA can now leverage its balance sheet, reducing dependence purely on donor replenishments
Risk: increased debt on IDA's own books — sustainability concerns and UPSC angle on why AAA is maintained

concepts.name: IDA's Special Financing Windows and Crisis Response Mechanisms
key_dimensions: Crisis Response Window (CRW): rapid financing for natural disasters and economic crises
Regional Integration Window: supports cross-border projects in Africa and other regions
Refugee Sub-Window: introduced in IDA18 to support countries hosting large refugee populations — novel and UPSC-relevant
Pandemic Emergency Financing Facility (PEF) linkage and IDA's role during COVID-19

concepts.name: IDA and Fragile and Conflict-affected States (FCS)
key_dimensions: Fragile States Facility within IDA: top-up allocations for FCS countries beyond Performance-Based Allocation
IDA's definition of fragility vs. UN classification — subtle trap for UPSC
Prevention and Resilience Allocation (PRA) introduced in IDA19 to address root causes of conflict
Turnaround Allocation: for countries transitioning out of fragility — IDA20 expanded this window

concepts.name: Performance-Based Allocation (PBA) System
key_dimensions: Country Policy and Institutional Assessment (CPIA): the scorecard that drives IDA allocations — components and critiques
IDA Performance-Based Allocation formula: relationship between CPIA score, portfolio performance, GNI per capita, and population
Debate: CPIA criticized for imposing donor-country governance norms on recipient countries
Small island economies exception: population floor ensures minimum allocations regardless of PBA score

concepts.name: India's Historical Relationship with IDA
key_dimensions: India as one of the largest historical recipients of IDA credits — relevance to India's development financing
India's graduation from IDA borrowing (formally stopped borrowing around 2014) — graduation criteria and process
India's transition to IDA donor status: contributing to IDA replenishments post-graduation
IDA projects in India: historical focus on rural development, infrastructure, health — legacy and lessons

concepts.name: IDA vs IMF Concessional Facilities: Distinguishing Mandates
key_dimensions: IDA vs IMF PRGT (Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust): both lend concessionally to poor countries but with different conditionalities
IDA focus: long-term development projects vs. IMF PRGT: balance of payments support — a common UPSC confusion zone
Debt Sustainability Framework (DSF): jointly developed by IDA and IMF for low-income countries
Interaction in debt crises: IMF program often precondition for IDA engagement — sequencing matters

concepts.name: IDA's Climate and Sustainability Agenda
key_dimensions: IDA20 commitment: 35% of financing to climate-related investments — largest climate commitment in IDA history
Climate Change Vulnerability Assessment linked to IDA allocations in small island states
'Blue Dot Network' and IDA's private sector mobilization for green infrastructure — geopolitical context
Just transition financing: IDA's role in helping fossil-fuel-dependent IDA countries transition sustainably

concepts.name: Debt Sustainability Framework (DSF) and IDA Grant Allocation
key_dimensions: DSF jointly operated by World Bank and IMF: classifies countries as low, moderate, high, or in debt distress
High debt distress → IDA provides 100% grants instead of credits — the automatic grant trigger mechanism
HIPC Initiative linkage: Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative and its interaction with IDA debt relief
Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative (MDRI): IDA cancelled 100% of debt owed by eligible HIPC countries — UPSC historical significance

concepts.name: IDA and Gender, Human Capital, and Social Development Priorities
key_dimensions: Human Capital Project (HCP): World Bank/IDA initiative measuring human capital index across IDA countries
Gender tag system: IDA projects must meet minimum gender-responsiveness standards in IDA18 onwards
IDA20 policy commitments: specific targets on gender-based violence, women's land rights, girls' education
Disability inclusion as a cross-cutting theme from IDA19 — less known, high UPSC potential

concepts.name: IDA's Role in Debt Relief Initiatives: HIPC and MDRI
key_dimensions: HIPC Initiative (1996, enhanced 1999): IDA as a key creditor providing debt relief — eligibility, decision point vs. completion point
MDRI (2006): IDA provided 100% debt cancellation to post-HIPC countries — distinction from HIPC partial relief is a trap
G20 Common Framework for Debt Treatment: IDA's role and limitations in coordinating with private creditors
Debt transparency agenda: IDA requirements for borrowers to disclose all public debt as conditionality

concepts.name: IDA Allocation to Africa and Regional Concentration Patterns
key_dimensions: Sub-Saharan Africa receives ~70% of IDA allocations — significance for understanding IDA's primary geographic focus
IDA Regional Window for Africa: supports regional public goods and cross-border infrastructure
Asia allocation: South Asia (Bangladesh, Pakistan, Ethiopia as top borrowers) — note India's absence post-graduation
Small Island Developing States (SIDS): special IDA provisions including vulnerability-based allocations

concepts.name: Private Sector Window (PSW) within IDA: Blended Finance Architecture
key_dimensions: PSW introduced in IDA18: uses concessional IDA resources to de-risk private investments in FCS and IDA-only countries
Four sub-windows: Blended Finance Facility, MIGA Guarantee Facility, Local Currency Facility, Risk Mitigation Facility
IFC-IDA nexus: PSW managed jointly — reflects 'cascade approach' of maximizing private finance before public
Critique: additionality concerns — whether PSW truly mobilizes new private capital or merely subsidizes existing flows

concepts.name: IDA Scorecard, Results Measurement, and Accountability Framework
key_dimensions: IDA Results Measurement System: Tier 1 (country outcomes), Tier 2 (IDA contribution), Tier 3 (operational effectiveness), Tier 4 (organizational capacity)
Independent Evaluation Group (IEG): evaluates IDA project outcomes — not part of IDA management, reports to Board
Inspection Panel: citizens of IDA-borrowing countries can file complaints — accountability mechanism UPSC often ignores
Disclosure policy: IDA's Access to Information Policy and exceptions — transparency vs. confidentiality balance

concepts.name: IDA and Pandemic/Health Financing Architecture
key_dimensions: IDA's role in health systems strengthening vs. WHO's normative role — complementarity and division of labor
COVID-19 Fast Track Facility under IDA: $160 billion committed over 15 months (2020–2021) — scale and speed
Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response (PPR) agenda in IDA20: dedicated allocation for health security
IDA's relationship with GAVI, Global Fund, and CEPI — IDA as financier vs. these bodies as fund managers

concepts.name: IDA's Concessional Terms Comparison: IDA vs ADF vs AsDF
key_dimensions: IDA vs African Development Fund (ADF): both concessional windows for Africa, but ADF is African Development Bank's arm — institutional trap
IDA vs Asian Development Fund (AsDF): Asian Development Bank's concessional window — similar structure, different governance
Interest rate and maturity comparison: IDA credits (0–1.25% service charge, 25–40 years) vs. ADF and AsDF terms
Coordination among MDB concessional windows: joint country partnership strategies to avoid duplication — UPSC policy angle
